posts.title: Low blood pressure: why it happens, what to do right away, and when not to wait
posts.excerpt: Under 90/60 with no symptoms isn't a disease. With dizziness and fainting, it is. The common causes, the steps that actually raise blood pressure within minutes, what doesn't help, and the short checklist for calling 112.
posts.author: Global Health Medical Team
posts.coverImageAlt: Woman sitting on a step in an apartment building hallway, holding a glass of water, with someone's hand on her shoulder, after a dizzy spell.
posts.seoTitle: Low blood pressure: causes, what to do, and when to call 112
posts.seoDescription: What low blood pressure means, the common causes, the steps recommended by the European guideline when you feel dizzy, why sugar water doesn't help, and when it's an emergency.

posts.title: How to lower blood pressure quickly: safe steps and when to call 112
posts.excerpt: There is no quick fix that is safe for everyone. Learn how to check a high reading, when to call 112 and why not to take extra captopril or another dose without a personal plan.
posts.author: Global Health Medical Team
posts.coverImageAlt: Woman repeats a blood-pressure reading at home while her family asks a doctor for advice by video.
posts.seoTitle: Lower blood pressure quickly: safe first steps
posts.seoDescription: What to do after a high reading, when to call 112 and why extra captopril, additional doses and improvised remedies may be unsafe.

posts.title: Normal blood pressure: a practical guide by age, without misleading tables
posts.excerpt: Which readings are genuinely normal in adults, why advancing age does not create a different ‘normal’, and when repeated high blood pressure should be discussed with a doctor.
posts.author: Global Health Medical Team
posts.coverImageAlt: Doctor and older patient review a home blood-pressure journal together in the consulting room.
posts.seoDescription: Learn which blood pressure readings are normal in adults, what changes with age, and when repeated high readings need medical review.

posts.title: The medical letter in Romania: who issues it, what it contains and what it is for
posts.excerpt: The scrisoare medicală is how a specialist tells your family doctor the diagnosis and the plan. Who may issue it, what it must contain, how long it stays valid and what to do when the one you were handed is incomplete.
posts.author: Global Health Medical Team
posts.coverImageAlt: Specialist completing a medical letter in two copies, stamp and ink pad on the desk and the patient seated opposite.
posts.seoTitle: Medical letter in Romania: who issues it
posts.seoDescription: The medical letter in Romania: who issues it, what it must contain, what it is used for, how long it is valid and what to do if it is incomplete.

posts.title: Chronic disease and Romania's national health programmes: how it works
posts.excerpt: The curative national health programmes cover treatment for serious chronic conditions: diabetes, oncology, cardiovascular and endocrine disease, rare diseases. How inclusion actually happens, which documents are involved, and what can be monitored online.
posts.author: Global Health Medical Team
posts.coverImageAlt: Patient measuring her blood pressure at the kitchen table and writing the readings in a notebook, weekly pill organiser beside her.
posts.seoTitle: Chronic disease and Romania's health programmes
posts.seoDescription: Diseases covered by Romania's national health programmes: what they include, how inclusion happens and how to monitor a chronic condition between reviews.

posts.title: Diabetes: The Silent Disease
posts.excerpt: Diabetes mellitus is one of the most widespread chronic diseases in Romania and one of the most underestimated. With the correct diagnosis, appropriate treatment and regular monitoring, people with diabetes can live full, healthy lives, especially thanks to recent advances such as GLP-1 receptor agonists and SGLT2 inhibitors.
posts.author: Global Health Medical Team
posts.seoTitle: Diabetes in Romania: Symptoms and Treatment
posts.seoDescription: More than 1.3 million Romanians live with diabetes, while many cases remain undiagnosed. Learn the causes, warning signs, treatments and future developments.
